gates.name: Player compatibility
gates.evidence: Live 2026-11-02: VISIONOS (no player script, no streaming token) answers OK with direct URLs for dQw4w9WgXcQ, and eXcor extracts from it. Its player request no longer sends youtube.com's Referer, which YouTube answers with 403. PlayerJsTest passes offline. Owner's PC, home network (Switzerland), 2026-11-03: the watch page loads (HTTP 200). Three bugs had kept the player-script path from ever starting, now fixed: the script URL is read from the page config (jsUrl, PLAYER_JS_URL) because the player response no longer carries assets.js; the 2.66 MB script exceeded the 2 MB fetch cap; and the EJS solver ran out of QuickJS memory at 64 MiB (it needs 256). The live player (sts 20754 and 20759) now solves: n and sig challenges both return answers, about 6 s cold. TVHTML5 then sends its player request, and YouTube answers it UNPLAYABLE (dQw4w9WgXcQ) or LOGIN_REQUIRED (kJQP7kiw5Fk)
blockers: No video was served to TVHTML5 on the owner's network either (UNPLAYABLE or LOGIN_REQUIRED), so no stream deciphered by the player script has been played. Cloud containers get a captcha instead of the watch page

gates.name: Streaming
gates.evidence: Live 2026-11-02 (LivePlaybackTest.extractedAudioDecodesFullyAndSeeks): eXcor extracted Opus/WebM audio for dQw4w9WgXcQ, the full 3,433,755-byte file decoded with ffmpeg without errors (213.06 s against a 213 s video), and a mid-file range read landed at the requested offset. The probe follows googlevideo's 302 to another allowlisted node. Video, live 2026-11-03 (LivePlaybackTest.extractedVideoAndAudioDecodeAndMux): extractVideo picked 480p H.264 (854x480, 14,103,519 bytes) and, with EXCOR_VIDEO_HEIGHT=1080, 1080p H.264 (1920x1080, 80,911,999 bytes) from VISIONOS; each was downloaded in 4 MiB range reads, muxed with its M4A audio by ffmpeg without re-encoding, fully decoded (213.09 s), and range-read from the middle. Rerun 2026-11-03 from a second cloud container: the audio decode, the 480p mux and the 27-format list pass again for dQw4w9WgXcQ. Owner's PC, home network, 2026-11-03: the same picture as the cloud: the 27-format list (144p to 2160p, all range-readable) and Opus audio for dQw4w9WgXcQ from VISIONOS; kJQP7kiw5Fk is LOGIN_REQUIRED on every client. ffmpeg was not installed, so the decode and mux tests were skipped there. PR #113 adds an experimental HLS manifest handoff; PR #114 connects it to Media3 in the Android preview. Their six-job CI verifies build/startup only: HLS live playback remains NOT RUN, child playlist and segment requests are host-player-managed, and no HLS decode/seek claim is made.
blockers: Most videos are still bot-checked or unavailable to every client from cloud containers (first session: kJQP7kiw5Fk unavailable; JGwWNGJdvx8, FGBhQbmPwH8, 9bZkp7q19f0 bot-checked. Second session, 2026-11-03: the same, and jNQXAC9IVRw and PkZNo7MFNFg bot-checked too), so publicMusicVideosReturnRangeReadableAudio fails on its second video there
The owner's home network and phone (mobile data) bot-check most videos too, so this is not specific to cloud IPs

gates.name: SABR/UMP
gates.evidence: No SABR network/playback transport. PRs #84, #86, #90 and #91 add only offline framing/response-assembly prototypes and synthetic bounds/continuation coverage; they do not implement or validate service negotiation, media decode or seeking. Closed issue #79 records the 2026-11-11 no-go decision: keep direct plus experimental HLS as interim scope and defer SABR until the independent contract, synthetic-vector and authorized audio/video decode-and-seek re-entry criteria in docs/UMP_FRAMING_RESEARCH.md are met. The bounded 2026-11-12 recheck in docs/UMP_G6_RECHECK_2026-11-12.md found no independently usable contract or authorized transport fixture in the checked primary sources and repository inventory; it does not claim global absence. G6 remains blocked; SABR/UMP playback 0/20.
blockers: No complete independently validated request/response contract, authorized playable stream, full decode, or seek evidence.

gates.name: YouTube Music
gates.evidence: Live: search with filters and continuations, suggestions, artist pages, playlists, radio; a top result card that plays is typed with its video ID (2026-11-03). Songs and albums are withheld from cloud containers (rechecked 2026-11-03). Owner's PC, home network, 2026-11-03: YouTube Music offers Songs and Albums there. LiveVideoInfoTest.youTubeMusicSongsAndAlbums passes: the Songs filter gives typed songs with video IDs, durations (now read from the subtitle; they were missing), album and artist links; the Albums filter gives albums whose playlists list their tracks; the artist page has a Top songs shelf and album shelves. Fixed on the way: the artist page's radio and shuffle playlist IDs, which YouTube now sends in a watchEndpoint
blockers: Discographies (an artist's full album list) are not covered by a live check yet

gates.name: Reliability
gates.evidence: Supported-target CI passed for merged PR #80 synthetic tests: bounded Retry-After/backoff, cancellation, declared/actual oversized responses, foreign media redirects and credential-safe logs. PR #81 adds session-generation invalidation for player, media and format results, also passing all six supported-target CI jobs. Live endpoint fault injection is still unverified. PR #102 adds bounded playback-profile exclusion eviction and refresh-recency regression tests (16 profiles per video; 256 videos); all six supported-target CI jobs passed exact head 5768cc2 in run 42999742743. The owner-operated JVM playback diagnostic shares a 256 MiB media-body budget across playback, probing and full decode; synthetic coverage verifies concurrent reservations and prompt child-process termination at the cap.
blockers: No owner-run fault-injection against an authorized live endpoint; synthetic coverage does not establish live playback reliability.
Two nulls in an earlier live run passed on reruns and have not been reproduced.

gates.name: Competitive analysis
gates.evidence: docs/COMPETITOR_MATRIX.md and docs/BLACK_BOX_COMPARISON_RESEARCH.md record public-documentation feasibility and version pins for eXcor, InnerTubeX, YouTube.js, and NewPipeExtractor without using or copying competitor implementation code. PR #117 adds an offline validator and JSONL/Markdown report aggregation; PR #118 adds a standalone eXcor JVM adapter; PR #122 adds the isolated GPL-3.0-or-later NewPipeExtractor v0.27.1 adapter and passed all six exact-head CI jobs in run 43102342730. PR #121 adds a standalone MIT YouTube.js adapter that selects direct-URL audio without player-code execution and bounds API/media bodies; all six jobs passed at exact head in run 43105597786. PR #120 adds the separate InnerTubeX v0.11.6 adapter; all six exact-head CI jobs passed in run 43109304794 at 4e4931cf1011fa8ad37acd89319798365593c59d. All adapters measure extraction and an initial media read; the eXcor/InnerTubeX JVM pair additionally supports optional bounded full decode with a shared FFmpeg version. PR #137 adds the paired full-decode path and passed all six supported CI jobs at exact head 6af9d8cff0e22de6592c114c06f71aa3db77729c in run 43153053461; it merged as ed0f64b5ff8bcf3389b5f4b9ecdbe0864a5b07a7. No matched comparative results are claimed. The owner-operated run_matched.py supplies shared comparison metadata, preflights adapters without requests, and validates sanitized outputs; its CI checks are offline. The YouTube.js V8 runtime is no longer mislabeled as a media decoder. No owner-run matched samples or player-seek results are claimed.
blockers: No matched owner-run comparative samples exist, including full decode and backward/forward seek measurements

gates.name: Security
gates.evidence: URL allowlist, safe data-class/log rendering, bounded responses and the shipped-dependency OSV scan remain in place. PR #87 merged as 3f451811af946e6d1253d81567d0399d622a4d5c after all six supported-target jobs passed in run 42965037745; it adds synthetic redaction coverage for transport/player diagnostics. G12 remains partial pending broader release-security evidence; Android lint findings are report-only and supplied by tooling dependencies. PR #103 (merged as ef5065b) removes session cookies and visitor IDs from direct media headers; all six supported-target CI jobs passed exact head 0b6be799 in run 43005770186. Signed-in playback remains unverified, and the release-security audit is incomplete. PR #104 merged as 752831b; the authorized-response cache guard passed all six supported-target CI jobs at exact head 80f0fdb1fa64a6e399c5cda88e5ccd7b1fe7bc13 in run 43009288965. The broader release-security audit remains incomplete. PR #105 merged as 860983b; the playback-reason redactor now removes X-Goog-Visitor-Id values, covered by a synthetic regression. All six supported-target CI jobs passed exact head 6dc35a73dc85c9ad14df235ca6eca3c64f33247 in run 43014757593. The broader release-security audit remains incomplete. PR #106 merged as `61de79b` after exact head `54585df2e3bf688181c0e2a8b3da3b5f2713499c` passed all six supported-target jobs in run 43022206848; the exclusion warning is static and accepts only a valid video ID as track ID, with a synthetic newline/credential-shaped regression. The broader release-security audit remains incomplete. PR #107 merged as `88fa980` after exact head `78395d6797f4773b518d053e0a2d26ecafdd88d8` passed all six supported-target jobs in run 43025409016; shared engine diagnostics now apply URL/credential redaction, control filtering, 200-character bounds, and valid video-ID track filtering, with a synthetic regression. The broader release-security audit remains incomplete. PR #108 merged as `9a01d03` after exact head `b4cd4ca079a25c125ccdda05ef3bdba0fd5e4562` passed all six supported-target jobs in run 43029076515; caller-facing player rejection exceptions now sanitize upstream reason text, with synthetic cookie, signed-URL and token redaction coverage. PR #124 merged as `e8b1af3080f94f8c30dc82581545de595d08dbb1` after exact head `3fa71184c0b01cb6bc7d12259b973ea1c6f268d8` passed all six supported-target jobs in run 43115947382; host-supplied session cookies, visitor data, region and language now have printable-ASCII and size bounds with synthetic regression coverage. PR #129 merged at 22958ca282a9279eb756e05d8425f6726072b474 after all six jobs passed at exact head in run 43130621290; the post-remediation OSV scan found no issues in 238 all-configuration packages or 115 shipped-runtime packages. The CI workflows now pin third-party actions to official release commit SHAs, apply `contents: read` to ordinary CI, and restrict the write-enabled score workflow's `workflow_run` job to pushes to this repository's `main`; monthly Dependabot checks action updates. G12 remains partial: the broader release-side security audit is incomplete, and the all-configuration tooling scan remains report-only.
